sampling_model.design: One known observational environment and one unknown-target stochastic perfect-intervention environment per latent node.
sampling_model.units: Independent observations within each of the \(n+1\) environments, split into ratio-training and evaluation folds.
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(i\) replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a positive parent-independent density; target labels are unknown and distinct.
sampling_model.overlap: All latent observational and interventional densities are strictly positive on the common compact cube.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Density ratios are fitted on training folds. The MMD theorem is conditional on its simultaneous evaluation-law \(L^1\) error event. The generated-rank question is separately conditional on the uniform \(C^1(K)\) log-ratio event \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\), with failure probability at most \(\eta_N\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Target knowledge: unknown. Interventions per node: one perfect stochastic intervention when \(n=2\), and two distinct paired perfect stochastic interventions for arbitrary \(n\). Mixing restriction: nonparametric invertible \(C^1\) mixing, including the paper's full \(\mathbb R^n\) setting. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: causally sufficient nonparametric mechanisms, with the ratio-law witness condition for the bivariate result. Graph or order input: neither is supplied. Recovered object: the latent graph and representation up to causal-representation equivalence.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 2 improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count on the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime. Its result for causal-minimal mechanisms is a separate structural extension within this note's regime and does not settle the comparator's full \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Target knowledge: unknown. Interventions per node: a complete family with at most one intervention per hidden variable. Mixing restriction: a latent-to-observed measurement DAG rather than a shared invertible map. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: nonparametric laws subject to the paper's marginal-independence, imaginary-subset, and isolated-edge graphical conditions. Graph or order input: neither the latent graph nor the number of hidden variables is supplied. Recovered object: a maximal measurement-model graph, only up to isolated latent edges, rather than latent coordinates.

Target knowledge: the intervened learned component and intervention value need not be known, and one distinct perfect do environment per latent yields recovery up to permutation. Interventions per node: one point-mass perfect do intervention. Mixing restriction: a finite-degree polynomial decoder with full-column-rank coefficient matrix, together with a polynomial learned decoder. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: no parametric latent law or DAG restriction, but observational and unintervened supports must have nonempty interior. Graph or order input: no graph or order is supplied. Recovered object: intervened latent coordinates up to permutation, shift, and scaling, not the causal DAG.

Target knowledge: unknown. Interventions per node: unknown-target perfect single-node intervention coverage. Mixing restriction: injective differentiable and otherwise general nonlinear mixing. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: a linear Gaussian latent SCM analyzed through precision-matrix quadratic geometry. Graph or order input: neither is supplied. Recovered object: the full latent model, intervention targets, and causal graph up to permutation and scaling.

Target knowledge: intervention targets are supplied in the main CauCA model. Interventions per node: one perfect stochastic intervention. Mixing restriction: arbitrary \(C^1\) diffeomorphic mixing. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: nonparametric causal mechanisms satisfying interventional discrepancy. Graph or order input: the full causal graph is supplied. Recovered object: the unmixing and latent mechanisms up to componentwise reparametrization.

Mixing restriction: smooth invertible encoders and decoders under the paper's invariance framework. Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: nonparametric latent mechanisms satisfying the stated invariance and sufficiency constraints. Graph or order input: a topological intervention-target order is supplied. Recovered object: elementwise latent components; the order itself is not recovered.

Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: nonparametric mechanisms with the paper's score-variability conditions. Graph or order input: neither is supplied. Recovered object: the latent variables and causal model through score-change structure.

Latent-SCM or mechanism restriction: additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic mechanisms with sufficient derivative changes. Graph or order input: neither is supplied. body.tldr: One unknown-target perfect intervention per latent node generically identifies an arbitrary finite nonlinear causal representation in the note's positive smooth compact-support, causal-minimal regime under shared diffeomorphic mixing. The observable ratio graph uses Gaussian-kernel MMD to compare the law of each observational-to-interventional likelihood ratio across environments; positive discrepancies on ancestral covers recover the transitive closure. Normalized affine interpolation toward a certified sparse edge witness makes this cover condition open dense in every nonempty causal-minimal derivative-sign stratum. Conditional ranks then recover componentwise coordinates and align intervention targets, while strict positivity and causal minimality make the true parent set the unique minimal ordered Markov boundary. On the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime, the result improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count of von Kugelgen et al. (2023); faithfulness is retained as a distinct stronger premise for that immediate corollary. The result does not settle their full \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class. A sample-split MMD theorem supplies simultaneous confidence edges conditional on its ratio-error event, while the generated-ratio conditional-CDF coordinate rate remains explicitly open.

project_justification.gap: The closest invertible-mixing nonparametric result proves one unknown-target perfect intervention per node only for two latents and uses two interventions per node in arbitrary dimension. On the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime, reducing that arbitrary-dimensional count to one is unresolved. The anchor also treats a broader \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class, which the present compact \(C^2\)-mixing theorem does not settle. Jiang and Aragam recover a latent measurement-model graph under different graphical assumptions; Ahuja et al. use point-mass interventions and polynomial support geometry; Buchholz et al. combine unknown targets and nonlinear mixing with a linear Gaussian latent SCM.
project_justification.niche: A mixing-invariant law of observed likelihood ratios can encode ancestry directly on environment labels, but its noncancellation must be derived inside normalized causal-minimal derivative-sign strata rather than assumed. Faithfulness remains a distinct stronger condition used only to state the immediate overlapping-regime corollary to the anchor.
project_justification.fill: The project proves ratio-specific open density by analytic interpolation on the causal-minimal stratum, decodes the full causal representation and exact DAG because causal minimality prunes parents under strict positivity, gives conditional simultaneous MMD confidence edges, and isolates generated-ratio conditional-CDF theory as the remaining statistical question. Its intervention-count comparison is confined to the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime and makes no claim for the anchor's full \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class.

body.related_work: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4 and Section 7) are the direct invertible-mixing comparator: targets are unknown, neither the graph nor an order is supplied, one perfect stochastic intervention per node identifies the graph and representation for two latents under a ratio-law witness, and the arbitrary-dimensional theorem uses two distinct paired interventions per node. On the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime, Theorem 2 improves that arbitrary-dimensional intervention count from two to one. Separately, the present theorem works in its own positive compact-support causal-minimal regime; this is a structural extension within the note's assumptions, not a claim to settle the comparator's full \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class. Faithfulness is retained as a distinct stronger premise for the immediate overlapping-regime corollary. Wendong et al. (2023, Theorem 4.2) use one target-aligned perfect stochastic intervention per node and arbitrary \(C^1\) diffeomorphic mixing with nonparametric mechanisms, but take the DAG and targets as inputs; on the relevant overlap, Theorem 2 recovers those supplied structural inputs. Yao et al. (2025, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1) similarly supply a topological target order. Jiang and Aragam (2023, Theorem 3.4) recover a maximal latent measurement-model graph, up to isolated latent edges, under marginal-independence, imaginary-subset, and isolated-edge conditions; they do not recover coordinates under shared invertible mixing, and neither model subsumes the other. Ahuja et al. (2023, Theorem 5.3) use one point-mass perfect intervention per latent and polynomial support geometry to recover intervened coordinates up to affine ambiguity, not the DAG; their assumptions are orthogonal to positive common-support stochastic interventions with arbitrary shared diffeomorphic mixing. Buchholz et al. (2023, Theorem 1) share unknown single-node targets and general nonlinear mixing but require a linear Gaussian latent SCM, again an incomparable regime. Var\i{}c\i{} et al. (2025, Theorem 29) use two uncoupled hard interventions per node under general transformations, while Ng et al. (2025, Theorems 1--2) use derivative-rich general environments with additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic latent restrictions. Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij (2026, Definition 4 and Lemmas 3--4) provide normalized conditional-kernel interpolation and faithfulness topology for a fixed DAG, but not the surgical density-ratio analytic contrast or mixed target assignment. Gretton et al. (2012, Theorems 5, 7, and 13) provide characteristicness and directly observed two-sample MMD concentration, not plug-in ratio graphs. Xie (2023, Theorems 1--3) and Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012, Theorem 1) provide complementary observed-argument and generated-covariate ingredients for the still-open generated-rank question. Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026, Theorems 4.6--4.7) study finite-sample recovery under high-dimensional linear factor mixing and unknown multi-node interventions, a different statistical regime.
body.interpretation: The genericity statement is topological: within every nonempty smooth compact-support causal-minimal fixed-sign stratum, the failure of cover-ratio separation is closed and nowhere dense. It is not a probability-one claim under an unspecified prior and supplies no uniform separation margin. Causal minimality is exactly sufficient for local path admissibility and parent pruning; full faithfulness gives an immediate stronger-class corollary but is not part of the primary identifying class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact cancellation mechanism with \(H'(x)=q_1(x)-1\) is faithful, hence also causal-minimal, and sign-valid, yet has \(D_{12}=0\). Thus even the stronger faithfulness condition plus monotone interventions does not imply ratio separation; the genericity theorem supplies no uniform positive MMD margin. Cover margins also do not control exact-parent uncertainty: an arbitrarily weak shortcut edge can be added to a chain while cover discrepancies remain separated.
body.honest_scope: The population open-density and exact-decoder claims are primary results for the note's positive smooth compact-support causal-minimal regime. Strict positivity supplies the intersection property used in parent pruning, and causal minimality makes the true parent set the unique minimal ordered Markov boundary. Faithfulness is preserved byte-for-byte as a distinct stronger assumption and yields an immediate corollary on the overlapping smooth compact-support faithful regime; only on that overlap does the note claim an arbitrary-dimensional intervention-count improvement relative to von Kugelgen et al. (2023). The note does not settle that anchor's full \(\mathbb R^n\)/\(C^1\) class. The all-DAG existence argument may use a terminating certified search rather than a closed-form family. The fixed-bandwidth MMD result remains conditional on its simultaneous first-stage \(L^1\) ratio-error event and does not provide a data-driven radius. The uniform own-derivative margin and bounded shared-mixing geometry are confined to the bounded Holder subclass and the generated-rank open question; they do not enter population genericity or exact decoding. The generated-rank question remains open: neither attainment nor sharpness of its proposed rate, nor the first-stage remainder required for a uniform asymptotically linear expansion, is claimed. Exact-parent inference under a separate conditional-dependence margin, noncompact supports, vector-valued nodes, imperfect interventions, and noninvertible observations remain outside the settled core. ROPES is only a protocol consumer after adopting a positive common-support intervention generator and a ratio-based estimator; its existing bounded additive-noise benchmark is not asserted to satisfy this model.
